findings.claim: The new context says MatchLimit and MatchLimitNoCase stop once the recursion counter exceeds maxcomp*len(str), to bound work on adversarial patterns. The repeat says the stopping condition matches match.go.
findings.reasoning: The summary omits the guard enabling the limit only for nonnegative maxcomp. A caller can pass a negative integer to either exported function; no input contract in the supplied source excludes it. Static inspection of MatchLimit("a", "a", -1) shows the limit check is skipped and matching proceeds; this example was not executed. Because the statement describes the work-limiting behavior of a public API, including adversarial-pattern use, the missing enabling condition changes its stated scope. This is evaluated under the frozen general claim-scope rubric, not a newly added required fact or a demand for exhaustive API documentation.
findings.effect: Fail the general supported-claims criterion for new-adopt and the repeat endorsement. The adopted rule, source-backed context usefulness and byte-preserving repeat still satisfy their separate target criteria.

limitations: One pinned public Go project with two author-created synthetic overlays and four dependent sessions; not four independent projects.
No ordinary-maintenance arm or reader phase; no comparative advantage, general reliability or reader-benefit inference.
Author-designed and author-reviewed, unblinded evaluation; counterpart review can adjudicate source judgments but does not make the study independent.
Restricted six-tool Claude Code configuration, explicit project-local skill invocation and one requested/responding model; no unrestricted-client or automatic-selection claim.
Effort is requested High, not independently observed. Loading events establish client-reported loading, not comprehension.
Mechanical and semantic results remain separate; frozen failures are retained without retries or post-hoc grading changes.
